title: Three Weeks and One Short Pencil
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：list　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 list 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the housekeeper ① made the list that no servant in the house would have recorded, and he said the making was the whole of the week. The ② list, meaning the record itself and not the pencil, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a list, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ list in that house had the same short pencil beside it, and the ④ list at the far door, meaning the name they kept for the children to add and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A list, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the housekeeper said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the list was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the record. The ⑥ list, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; list, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a record and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ list had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short pencil. The ⑧ list of the whole thing, the housekeeper wrote in May, was one house and three weeks of recording; list, he said, is either the name at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ list I remember is the record recorded in the ledger, which closed in 1966 and is still recorded as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ list, my mother said in 1968, is the only record that improves by being recorded; every list, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a record. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 清单；名单（指宅子里每一张旁边的那一张）
B. n. 清单；名单（指那张清单本身，与铅笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the list 列出这张清单
D. n. 清单；名单（指留给孩子们添上的那个名字那一张）
E. n. 记事之事（抽象总称，指一处宅子的清单之事）
F. n. 清单；名单（指家用账簿里写到、被记载的的那一张）
G. n. 次序、条理（指一件事里人人都记却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 条理（抽象总称，指人人都记却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: make the list 意为“列出这张清单”，1959 年那位管家把宅子里没有一位佣人肯记载的一张清单做了一遍。
list 意为“清单；名单”，指那张清单本身而不是铅笔，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记载。
list 意为“清单；名单”，指宅子里每一张旁边的那一张，每一张旁边都有同一支短短的铅笔。
list 意为“清单；名单”，指最远那扇门后留给孩子们添上的那个名字那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
list 意为“次序、条理”，指一件事里人人都记却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个次序就是那件事的全部。
list 意为“条理”，指人人都记却无人提起的那样东西而不是那张清单，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
list 意为“清单；名单”，指家用账簿里写到、被记载的的那一张，到 1964 年这一张成了家用账簿里的一行。
list 意为“记事之事”，管家五月写道，整件事的清单之事是一处宅子和三个星期的记载。
list 意为“清单；名单”，我记得的是家用账簿里记载过的那一张，1966 年列好了，至今仍被说成宅子里最安静的一张。
list 为抽象总称，母亲 1968 年说，清单是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的清单。
